script.analysis: All 20,009 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: social media comparison and generic-cereal joke; subscribe/like CTA. Sections: about one in three carry credit-card debt at 20-30%; nearly 40% have side hustles averaging ~$800/month; selective spending trade-offs (traveler in thrift clothes, house-rich peanut-butter lunches); fake-it-till-you-make-it performance; social-media highlight reels; quiet real wealth; different starting points and timing luck; $1,000 emergency fragility; dollars as employees; instant vs delayed gratification; BMW friend shuffling card balances; family financial support as stealth advantage; savers happier; advertising and social-media consumption arms race; close: stop comparing to highlight reels. Observational, joke-heavy monologue without data visualization, few sourced numbers, one anecdote and repetitive phrasing; balanced acknowledgment of structural advantages. ASR noise ("you're over whether here calculating", "bake your noodle") preserved; not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:10000 "Roughly one in three Americans carry credit-card debt" is in the range of survey estimates of adults revolving balances (unsourced). Card APRs 20-30% plausible for 2025. "Fancy dinner will cost double by the time they pay it off" requires years of minimum payments at ~22%; overstated as a general claim. "Nearly 40% have a side hustle averaging ~$800/month" resembles Bankrate side-hustle surveys (~36%, several hundred dollars monthly); unverified exact.

10000:20009 "Huge percentage can't cover $1,000" consistent with Bankrate-type surveys. "Research consistently shows savers are happier" is directionally supported by liquid-savings well-being studies but unsourced here. Family support and starting conditions acknowledged accurately as advantages. BMW card-shuffling acquaintance is an unverifiable persona anecdote. No tax or product claims.
